_comment: Mutations that break the Google REDIRECT sign-in flow, one at a time.
Every mutation must be caught by frontend/src/__tests__/googleRedirectSignIn.test.tsx.
This spec has no pytest target: the flow is front-end only and its tests
are run by vitest. The harness accepts a 'command' for exactly that case,
and keeps every other guarantee it already had -- snapshot before, SHA-256
revert verification after, and a SKIP counts as a failure.
The server half of the same flow (single-use enforcement, and the rule
that a credential is never logged) is a SEPARATE spec with a pytest
NEVER run concurrently with a test run or tools/review_fanout.py -- both will
read a file that is mid-mutation and report on code that does not exist.

Mutants AA-AE cover the ways the Google link can be followed (a middle click, the context menu, a ctrl/cmd+click) and the rule that a failure which is not ours must not destroy a sign-in that is still in flight.

The command runs vitest with --bail=1: a mutation that makes a test fail also made vitest hang (the event loop is blocked, so even the test timeout cannot fire), and a hang leaves the harness with NO verdict. Bailing at the first failing test keeps the verdict -- a mutation is caught by ONE failing test -- and always prints the summary.

Mutants AJ and AK cover the two halves of the LOOP DEFENCE: the handler's memory of the response it has already reported, and the store that keeps ONE attempt per sign-in. A hang is a FAILURE, not a pass: the command carries vitest's own test and hook timeouts, and the spec's timeout_s is short, so a mutant that blocks the event loop is stopped and reported as INCONCLUSIVE -- which the harness counts as a failure.

mutations.label: A: the redirect URI gains a trailing slash (Google rejects it with redirect_uri_mismatch)
mutations.replace: export const GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI = "https://depthsight.diverseinc.net/";  // MUTANT

mutations.label: B: the flow asks for an auth code, so no credential ever arrives in the fragment
mutations.replace: response_type: "code",  // MUTANT

mutations.label: C: the email scope is dropped
mutations.replace: export const GOOGLE_SCOPE = "openid profile";  // MUTANT

mutations.label: D: the browser is sent somewhere other than Google's authorization endpoint
mutations.replace:
export const GOOGLE_AUTHORIZE_ENDPOINT =
	"https://example.invalid/o/oauth2/v2/auth";  // MUTANT

mutations.label: E: the credential is left in the address bar and in the browser history

			return;

mutations.replace:
const at = typeof parsed.at === "number" ? parsed.at : 0;
	if (Date.now() - at > PENDING_MAX_AGE_MS) return null;  // MUTANT: an aged marker is dropped

mutations.replace: // MUTANT: the state is never compared

mutations.replace: fail(t("googleSignInUnverified"));  // MUTANT: the wrong message

mutations.replace: if (false) {  // MUTANT: a stale marker is treated as fresh

mutations.label: S: the marker is not written to the SHARED store, so a sign-in that comes back in another tab is rejected
mutations.replace: // MUTANT: the marker is not written to the shared store

mutations.label: T: the SHARED store is never read, so a sign-in that comes back in another tab is rejected
mutations.replace: : null;  // MUTANT: the shared store is never read

mutations.label: U: a browser that blocks storage is not reported, so the sign-in fails in silence
mutations.replace: // MUTANT: an unavailable storage is not reported

mutations.label: V: the sign-in starts even when the marker cannot be recorded, so it is guaranteed to be rejected on the way back
mutations.replace: if (!rememberPendingGoogleRequest(googleSignIn.state, follow) && false) {

mutations.label: W: the claim never refuses a second attempt, so a reload sends the credential twice
mutations.replace: // MUTANT: the claim never refuses a second attempt

mutations.label: X: the one-time value is not sent to the server, so the server cannot consume it once
mutations.replace: // MUTANT: the one-time value is not sent

mutations.label: Y: every attempt carries the SAME one-time value, so the server refuses the user's second attempt
mutations.replace: nonce: "the-same-one-time-value",  // MUTANT

mutations.label: Z: a new attempt does not supersede the previous claim, so the user cannot sign in again
mutations.replace: // MUTANT: the previous claim is never superseded

mutations.label: AA: the marker is written only on a primary click again, so a middle click or the context menu cannot sign in
AB: a failure that is not ours destroys the marker, so the sign-in that is still in flight is refused
AC: an unrelated page load destroys the SHARED copy of the marker, so the credential that comes back later is refused
mutations.replace:
removePendingAttempt("tab", state);
	removePendingAttempt("shared", state);  // MUTANT: an unrelated page load destroys the shared copy of the marker

mutations.label: AD: the credential stays in the address bar when it has already been sent
AE: a ctrl/cmd+click claims the sign-in in the tab that stayed behind
mutations.replace: "tab",  // MUTANT: a ctrl/cmd+click claims the sign-in in the tab that stayed behind

mutations.label: AF: the keyboard's context menu does not record the sign-in, so Shift+F10 cannot sign in
AG: the attempt is not selected by its state, so a credential is matched to the WRONG sign-in
mutations.replace: if (attempts[index]) return attempts[index];  // MUTANT: the state is not compared

mutations.label: AH: removing the consumed attempt wipes every attempt in the store, so the other sign-in that is still in flight is refused
mutations.replace: const kept: PendingAttempt[] = [];  // MUTANT: the removal wipes every attempt in the store

mutations.label: AI: the expired cleanup destroys the SHARED copy of the marker, so the credential that comes back later is refused
mutations.replace:
removePendingAttempt("tab", request.state);
	removePendingAttempt("shared", request.state);  // MUTANT: the expired cleanup destroys the shared copy too

mutations.label: AJ: the handler does not remember that it already reported a response, so the same failure is reported twice
mutations.needle:
// This response is reported ONCE.
			handledRef.current = responseKey;

mutations.label: AK: the store keeps ONE attempt, so a second sign-in destroys the first one (the single shared slot)
mutations.needle:
const kept = attempts.filter((entry) => entry.state !== attempt.state);
	kept.push(attempt);
mutations.replace:
const kept: PendingAttempt[] = [];  // MUTANT: the store keeps a single attempt
	kept.push(attempt);
